title: David of Sassoun
author: Armenian oral epic tradition
short_summary: David of Sassoun is the great Armenian folk epic about a boy raised in the mountain land of Sassoun who grows into its fiercest defender. Wielding his father's sword, Lightning, and riding his fire-colored horse Kurkik Jalali, David stands up to the powerful Caliph of Baghdad's army, which has long forced Sassoun to pay a heavy tribute. In a final duel with the invading commander Msra Melik, David's courage frees his homeland for good.
extended_summary:
David of Sassoun is the third branch of a much longer Armenian epic passed down for centuries by storytellers before it was written down. The full epic follows several generations of heroes: the twin founders Sanasar and Baghdasar, who build the fortress of Sassoun; their son Mher the Elder; and finally David, the boy who grows up an orphan, underestimated by nearly everyone around him because he seems clumsy and simple. As David grows, his true strength emerges, and he inherits his father's sword, Lightning (Tur Kaputkin), along with the loyal horse Kurkik Jalali, who can sense danger before David does.

When the Caliph of Baghdad sends his commander Msra Melik to collect the unfair tribute that has burdened Sassoun for years, David refuses to let his people be bullied any longer. He challenges Msra Melik to single combat rather than allow a war that would cost countless lives. Through clever strength, patience, and belief in the justice of his cause, David defeats Msra Melik and ends the tribute forever, becoming the beloved hero-protector of Sassoun and a lasting symbol of Armenian resilience.

The tribute was a voluntary gift of friendship
Sassoun owed money for building its fortress

questions.explanation: The tribute began generations earlier as a way to avoid conflict, but over time it became an unfair burden that David refuses to keep paying.

Because Sassoun had no army left
Because Msra Melik demanded it as a game

questions.explanation: David chooses single combat to settle the conflict directly and spare his people the losses of a full-scale war.
